statedReasoning: Per the fully-fetched důvodová zpráva (both the Obecná and Zvláštní část), the bill remedies the situation of so-called "uzamčení účastníci" (locked-in participants) of the third pension pillar. Law č. 462/2023 Sb. (rozvoj finančního trhu / podpora zajištění na stáří, promulgated 29 Dec 2023, effective for this purpose from 1 July 2024) removed the státní příspěvek (state contribution) for participants of doplňkové penzijní spoření (427/2011) and older penzijní připojištění (42/1994) who had been granted an old-age pension. It applied retroactively to existing contracts but gave those participants no penalty-free exit: those not meeting the conditions for jednorázové vyrovnání (lump-sum settlement) could only leave via odbytné (losing already-credited state contributions) or, in extreme cases, lose their own funds entirely. The Constitutional Court (nález Pl. ÚS 18/24, 29 Jan 2025) held the removal itself constitutional but noted the legislature may still create relief. This bill provides that relief with two measures: (1) a new §28a in Law 427/2011 grants ~150,000 still-enrolled locked-in participants (those who contracted before 29 Dec 2023 and later lost the state contribution due to old-age-pension award) the right to a jednorázové vyrovnání — a full penalty-free exit — even though they do not meet the general §24(1)(a) conditions; and (2) transitional provisions (Čl. II) under which the Ministry of Finance returns, on written request within a 6-month preclusive deadline, the state contribution lost by the ~16,000 participants who had already exited with financial consequences, and the pension company returns the own funds of the ~100 who lost even those. The income-tax law 586/1992 is amended (§15b(1)(a)(1) adds the age-60 condition; §15b(4)(a) adds a new clawback exception) so that using this new exit does not strip the product of its tax-advantaged status, and Čl. IV transitional provisions exempt the returned own funds from personal income tax and prevent taxation of employer contributions on these lump sums. Stated fiscal impact: ~60 million CZK from the state budget (the DZ expressly notes not all eligible will claim), no impact on other public budgets. Sponsors requested (unsuccessfully) an expedited single-reading and a non-standard effective date (first day of the month after promulgation) so relief reaches participants quickly. Predkladatelé identified no lobbyists under the lobbying-regulation law.
researchedContext: The psp.cz legislative history confirms the print was submitted 27 Feb 2026, received a government approval statement (souhlasné stanovisko, 10 Mar 2026), was assigned the rozpočtový výbor (Budget Committee) as garanční/guarantor committee with rapporteur Vladimír Pikora, passed first reading on 24 Mar 2026 (the Chamber rejecting the proposers' expedited single-reading), was recommended by the Budget Committee (7 Apr 2026), passed third reading 27 May 2026, was approved by the Senate (8 Jul 2026), signed by the President (16 Jul 2026), and — per the psp.cz history page — was promulgated in the Collection of Laws in July 2026. The amended statutes are both real and correctly identified: 427/2011 Sb. governs doplňkové penzijní spoření (the post-2013 third-pillar product), and 586/1992 Sb. is the income-tax act; the DZ situates both within the voluntary, individually-contracted third pension pillar (also comprising penzijní připojištění under 42/1994, penzijní pojištění, life insurance and the DIP long-term investment product). The measure is a targeted consumer-remedy correcting an unintended harshness of the 2023 finance-market package; it is non-EU-harmonised national competence. Nothing in the researched record indicates a hidden industry beneficiary — the direct beneficiaries are a diffuse population of ~166,000 ordinary pension savers, and pension companies act only as administrators returning funds they held or owed.

unstatedEffects.effect: Compensation for the ~16,000 already-exited participants is opt-in and gated by a 6-month preclusive (prekluzivní) deadline (Čl. II bod 2): eligible former savers who never learn of the law or miss the window permanently forfeit the returned state contribution. The DZ itself budgets for incomplete uptake ("je pravděpodobné, že žádost o vrácení státního příspěvku nepodají úplně všichni"), so the ~60M CZK estimate presupposes that a share of entitled people will not be paid; unclaimed amounts stay with the state. This distributional consequence — relief conditioned on the least-informed acting fastest — is presented by the DZ only as administratively necessary, not as a foreseeable under-payment.
unstatedEffects.whoBenefits: The state budget (retains unclaimed compensation); disadvantages the least-informed former participants who miss the 6-month opt-in window.

conflictAssessment: Negligible; the honest finding is the absence of a conflict, not a scandal. This is a remedial, pro-saver bill that returns money to a diffuse population of roughly 166,000 ordinary third-pillar pension participants disadvantaged by an earlier law, at a modest ~60M CZK cost to the state, with no identifiable private-industry beneficiary. The sponsors' graph-linked money ties do not connect to the bill's subject (third-pillar supplementary pension savings and its income-tax treatment): Patrik Nacher's largest tie, Operátor ICT, a.s. (~884.9M CZK), is Prague's municipal IT/e-government company; Boris Šťastný's largest tie, Pražské služby a.s. (~1.47bn CZK), is Prague's municipal waste-management operator (his other ties GEKO SPORT and VZP are a sports entity and the public health insurer — neither a penzijní společnost); Tomio Okamura's tie MIKI TRAVEL PRAGUE (~6.05M CZK) is a travel firm. None of these is a pension company, asset manager, or provider of a tax-advantaged retirement-savings product, so there is no plausible channel from this bill to any sponsor-linked revenue. Lead sponsor Alena Schillerová is a former Finance Minister; her authorship of a fix to the 2023 finance-market package is a policy/political fact, not a financial self-dealing conflict. Symmetric across the five sponsors (ANO, SPD, independents): money ties exist but none touch the regulated sector, a valid low-severity outcome.

citations.claim: Tisk 119 amends Law 427/2011 (new §28a granting locked-in participants a penalty-free jednorázové vyrovnání, plus §191a and Čl. II transitional provisions returning lost state contributions to ~16,000 exited participants and own funds to ~100) and Law 586/1992 (§15b(1)(a)(1) age-60 condition, §15b(4)(a) new clawback exception, Čl. IV tax exemptions); the full důvodová zpráva states the ~150,000 still-enrolled and ~16,000 exited figures, the ~60M CZK fiscal estimate with acknowledged incomplete uptake, the Pl. ÚS 18/24 ruling, and the 6-month preclusive claim deadline. Signed by Schillerová, Nacher, Šťastný, Okamura, Malá, Prague 26 Feb 2026.
The amended supplementary-pension-savings statute is zákon č. 427/2011 Sb., o doplňkovém penzijním spoření — a real, in-force Czech law.
The amended income-tax statute is zákon č. 586/1992 Sb., o daních z příjmů — a real, in-force Czech law.

The law that removed the state contribution for third-pillar participants granted an old-age pension (the harm this bill remedies) is zákon č. 462/2023 Sb.; it is listed among the amending laws of 427/2011 in the bill text itself and is a real Czech law.
